articles.title: South Africa v Australia: second men’s cricket Test, day one delayed by rain – live
articles.summary: Updates as the Proteas host Australia at St George’s Park. Play start time in Gqeberha is 10am local/7pm AEDT/9am BST. Any thoughts? Get in touch with an email. I like all the changes for South Africa.
body: I like all the changes for South Africa. It’s great that Tristan Stubbs wants to be a Test player, given all his attention from the franchise circuit, but he didn’t look up to speed in Durban, where Breetzke really did take it up to the Aussies in the one-day series, and looked to have a lot to offer technically as well as in attitude.

Ackerman has a monster first-class record and has earned a shot at the next level up, and to make space for him the move involved getting Rickelton out of the opening spot, which he desperately needs based on the evidence of Durban, then having him go down the order to become the keeper in place of Verreyne, who was dreadful last start and hasn’t made runs in any Test for a while.

Then Rabada coming in speaks for itself, although Maharaj has historically taken the fight up to the Australians, so I’d have expected him to stay as the lone spinner. But glad to see Harmer get another chance to show his quality.
So the hosts look stronger up top, stronger in the middle, and stronger as a bowling outfit. It may all fail terribly, but it’s a nice setup before a ball is bowled.

articles.title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One
articles.summary: Gary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than Saturday’s win over Reading to disperse the clouds. If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for…
body: The club, perhaps understandably, continue to hark back to their halcyon days. Last season they brought back Gary Caldwell – club captain in 2013 – for his second stint as manager, having led the club to promotion from this division in 2015-16. Choosing to swap Exeter for a return to the Latics last season was seen as a risky move by Caldwell, considering the shoestring budget imposed upon him by Mike Danson, the owner who is keen to sell.

Finances are ultra-tight at the Greater Manchester club amid dwindling crowds and losses on the pitch and on the balance sheet. The local businessman Danson and his family saved Wigan from liquidation in June 2023 after mismanagement from previous owners brought a points deduction and relegation from the Championship. Three successive mid-table finishes in League One under their stewardship have brought a semblance of stability, but this season they have plummeted.

articles.title: New Zealand avoid World Cup shock against Fiji
articles.summary: New Zealand women are given a World Cup "wake-up call" after they are forced to come from behind to beat debutants Fiji in their opening game.
body: The Ferns are one of the most successful teams in women's rugby league history – they have reached the final of all six World Cups, winning the first three before finishing runners up to Australia in the previous three years.
They are generally considered second favourites this time around and were expected to win easily against the Fijians in Newcastle on Sunday.
Instead, New Zealand were made to battle to an 18-12 win, having trailed 12-4 in the first half.
They were 12-10 down at the break – the first time they have ever been behind at half-time in a World Cup match.

articles.title: ‘I suffer a lot’: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig on not enjoying games and the prospect of Liverpool
articles.summary: It will be a tense time for club’s president despite the Champions League game at Anfield offering a symbol of how far they have come. The first time Fernando Roig watched Villarreal play as their president, he sat in the stand at a tiny whitewashed ground that had concrete fever and was half…
body: But then, he doesn’t ever enjoy it much. Even on Tuesday at Anfield, he will not: into his 30th year, the longest presidency in Europe, that is about the only thing that hasn’t changed. More than 1,000 games and still it happens. “I don’t get nervous. It’s worse: I get worried, very anxious,” he says. “I suffer a lot.

“It’s emotional to play Liverpool. This will be the fifth time we have faced them, the third at Anfield. The other two were European semi-finals. I’ll watch the morning training session, travel with the team. We’ll go and eat; everywhere we go we get treated very well and we treat them well back. The next day I’ll watch the under-19s in the morning, that I do like. And then the game, which I don’t. Then we’ll fly back here very, very late. It’s very stressful.”

It is the morning after Villarreal have beaten Napoli in the Champions Leagueand Roig is in an office at the headquarters of Pamesa, the ceramics company he owns, on the edge of town. He is better now, the tension subsided. They needed that victory, their first in the competition going back to before they last faced Liverpool, in the 2022 semi-final, and, besides, he is always better the next day.

articles.title: Do Manchester City have any grounds to win their appeal?
articles.summary: Manchester City face "substantial hurdles" to overcome if they are to have any chance of winning their appeal after being found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules, a leading lawyer has told BBC Sport.
body: City have been found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and creating "sham contracts" to inflate sponsorship deals by £830m.

The club have said they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and they have "irrefutable evidence" the ruling "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe".
In their appeal, City will argue the payments were made by the United Arab Emirates government as a shareholder of the sponsors, while there are inconsistencies in the Commission's judgement.
Therefore, City say the sponsorship amounts were legitimate and not topped up by the owners.

articles.title: Kirby 'stressed' by abrupt Vidosic exit from Brighton
articles.summary: Former England striker Fran Kirby says the departure of Brighton head coach Dario Vidosic on the eve of the season left her feeling "stressed" and "disappointed".
body: Vidosic guided Brighton to the club's first FA Cup final this year and finished a club-record fifth and seventh in the Women's Super League before leaving abruptly on 28 August, nine days before their opener against Arsenal.
He was replaced by Real Sociedad manager Arturo Ruiz on the same day.
"It wasn't easy when I heard," Kirby told the Women's Football Weekly podcast. "I was a bit disappointed.
"I had a really good relationship with Dario and think he's a fantastic coach that can go on and achieve amazing things with top clubs.

articles.title: 3 takeaways from Utah’s tough win over Colorado
articles.summary: Perhaps it was a little closer than most Utah fans expected, or wanted it to be, but Morgan Scalley’s team gutted out a victory over Deion Sanders and Colorado, 27-24, on Saturday.
body: It was a sneaky quiet night for Wayshawn Parker with 98 yards rushing and no touchdowns, but Devon Dampier brought the arm power that accounted for 278 yards through the air and three touchdowns that ultimately was too much for Isaac Wilson and his team’s third-quarter surge that allowed the Buffaloes to take the lead.
The former Utah quarterback accounted for 256 yards passing but threw a late interception that ended up costing Colorado as Utah took a 10-point lead.

With the ball sitting at the Colorado 3-yard line in the first half, it seemed Utah was bound to punch the ball into the end zone. But instead, Buffalo defensive lineman Dylan Manuel found it in his hands after a shovel pass from Dampier got tipped backward.

The Utes have benefited mightily by keeping defenses on their toes this season, but with that comes some risk, something Dampier and offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven learned a few yards from six points, then again in the fourth quarter on back-to-back plays.

articles.title: It's official, Liverpool pulled off incredible bargain
articles.summary: Liverpool have pulled off an incredible bargain that nobody noticed. Richard Hughes is unlikely to look back on his time at Anfield with much credit. His recruitment strategy has left Liverpool with a squad that feels disjointed, raising serious questions about the balance between individual…
body: The Reds have invested heavily in high-profile players, sometimes seemingly paying over the odds for names who have yet to justify their price tags. However, judging Hughes' legacy now would be premature. His signings must be assessed over the long term, particularly if the intention was to build a squad capable of competing for years to come.

Rebuilding takes time, but that makes recruitment even more important. Hughes wanted elite talent, yet signing the best players means little if they don't complement each other or fit the team's tactical requirements.

You can debate Florian Wirtz’s performances all you want, but one thing is clear: Liverpool have an incredibly young squad, and arguably one of the most exciting groups of young talent in world football.

The Reds might not be among Europe’s elite just yet, but that was never going to happen overnight. There are still a few key signings needed before this squad feels complete, and patience will be crucial.
points: Liverpool have pulled off an incredible bargain that nobody noticed.
Richard Hughes is unlikely to look back on his time at Anfield with much credit.
The Reds have invested heavily in high-profile players, sometimes seemingly paying over the odds for names who have yet to justify their price tags.
However, judging Hughes' legacy now would be premature.

articles.title: Van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Van Veen makes history
articles.summary: Dutch favourite Michael van Gerwen suffered a shock second-round exit at the Dutch Darts Championship on Saturday, losing 6-5 to Irishman William O'Connor.
body: The defeat extends Van Gerwen's poor run of form, having lost his opening match at four European Tour events this season before arriving in Maastricht: the European Darts Trophy, German Darts Grand Prix, Flanders Darts Trophy and Swiss Darts Trophy. It marks his most first-round exits in a single season since the tour began in 2012.
O'Connor produced a superb display, firing in three ton-plus checkouts of 136, 131 and 121 to seal his victory and book his place in round three.
Elsewhere on Saturday, Gerwyn Price's return to the stage ended in glory as he beat Scott Williams 6-3, while Gian van Veen broke the European Tour record average.
Martin Schindler and Stephen Bunting also jumped into the qualification spots for Dortmund.

articles.title: ‘Incredible’: Nottingham Forest boss praises Arsenal ahead of match
articles.summary: Oliver Glasner has heaped praise on Arsenal ahead of Nottingham Forest’s match against the Gunners this weekend, highlighting the talent and hard work in Mikel Arteta’s squad. Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images.
body: Arsenal return to Premier League action this weekend with a match away to Nottingham Forest on Sunday, and Forest boss Oliver Glasner will be facing the Gunners for the first time in charge of his new club.

It hasn’t been too long since Glasner has managed a team against Arsenal though, as he was in charge of Crystal Palace for the final Premier League match of last season, watching Mikel Arteta’s side lift the trophy at the end of the game.
Glasner has evidently watched Arsenal in action a few more times since then, and he had plenty of praise for the Gunners in his pre-match press conference.
“In every game this season they were outrunning the opposition,” Glasner pointed out. “It’s incredible. The effort and the mindset Mikel [Arteta] has created there is incredible.

articles.title: Williams stars as Golden State Valkyries beat Atlanta Dream in WNBA Finals Game 1
articles.summary: Gabby Williams converted two free throws with 1:18 left to put Golden State ahead, two more with 4.1 seconds to go, and finished with 26 points as the Valkyries held off the Atlanta Dream 68-64 in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals.
body: Williams scored 16 of her points in the second quarter and no other Valkyries reached double figures as they shot 32.1 per cent and seven of 33 from three-point range.
"We always knew we were going to find a way somehow," Williams said on the microphone postgame as fans chanted "Gabby! Gabby!"
Rhyne Howard missed a three-point attempt with 1:09 left, but Angel Reese made a steal moments later.
Naz Hillmon missed from deep, Kiah Stokes missed the first of two free throws with 23.8 seconds left, and then Allisha Gray missed a three with nine seconds left.

articles.title: Rangers miss chance to go top as Jones earns Dundee a point
articles.summary: Callum Jones scored a second-half equaliser as Rangers were held to a 2-2 draw by Dundee and missed the chance to go top of the Scottish Premiership.
body: Dundee opened the scoring when Rangers failed to deal with a routine long ball, with Bradley Fink capitalising to round the goalkeeper and slide home.
The lead did not last long, though, as Badredine Bouanani cut inside and curled in a stunning equaliser to open his account for Rangers.
Nico Raskin scored the goal of the game when his shot from outside the area went in off the underside of the crossbar.
But Jones then caught Dan Neil dwelling on the ball and nicked it off the Rangers captain to slot home the Dundee equaliser.
